challengePass.question: Could Ferrum become materially faster or easier for agents by switching ref semantics or adopting compact/delta snapshots immediately?
challengePass.result: No second product change cleared the proof gate. Fresh-per-snapshot refs would discard useful stable identity without measured benefit. Compact/delta snapshots are promising but require a same-workload payload/tool-call benchmark with the complete raw snapshot still available. The next experiment therefore measures optional derived deltas rather than changing default evidence or ref semantics.

nextExperiments: Benchmark an optional derived compact/delta snapshot inspired by graph-memory/browser-mcp while always retaining the complete raw snapshot; measure response bytes, tool calls, elapsed time, success and evidence completeness.

Build a dynamic-SPA ref lifecycle benchmark covering insertion, reorder, rerender, duplicate page-authored refs, stale refs and tab isolation; compare Ferrum persistent refs with epoch-qualified or runtime-owned alternatives before changing semantics.
Add token/schema burden accounting to the agent-tool benchmark and compare Ferrum CLI/MCP profiles with Playwright MCP and Playwright CLI/skills on identical tasks.
After snapshot/ref experiments converge, rotate to the next unreviewed adapter/diagnostic category rather than repeating settled candidates.
guardrails: No viewport-only shortcuts, caps, reduced snapshots, skipped targets, stale caches, weaker tests, or reduced diagnostic fidelity.
Compact/delta outputs may only be additive derived views until full raw evidence remains available and parity is proven.
No external browser-agent dependency replaces Ferrum's deterministic control path without identical-workload evidence and full acceptance parity.
